title: Using Five‑Blade Scissors to Make Herb‑Packed Summer Slaw
meta_description: Discover a fresh herb packed summer slaw recipe that maximizes flavor using five‑blade herb scissors—easy, crisp, and perfect for warm weather gatherings.
html:
When the heat rolls in, a bright, crunchy slaw is the ultimate side dish. This herb packed summer slaw recipe leans on the power of fresh cilantro, chives, and basil, all minced in seconds with the five‑blade Herb Scissors. The result is a salad that bursts with garden‑fresh herbs, vibrant veggies, and a tangy dressing that ties everything together.

Why Five‑Blade Herb Scissors Change the Game

Traditional herb prep—chopping with a knife, then gathering the pieces—creates a lot of waste and uneven cuts. The five‑blade Herb Scissors mince cilantro, chives, and basil in one snip, delivering uniformly fine pieces that distribute evenly through the slaw. The built‑in cleaning comb makes cleanup a breeze, so you can jump from prep to plating without a mess.

Ingredients for a Herb Packed Summer Slaw

All ingredients are pantry staples, but the herbs are the star. Feel free to adjust quantities to suit your taste or the size of your crowd.

  • 1 small head green cabbage, finely shredded (about 4 cups)
  • 1 small red cabbage, finely shredded (about 2 cups)
  • 2 large carrots, julienned or grated
  • 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves
  • ½ cup fresh chives, trimmed
  • ¼ cup fresh basil leaves
  • ¼ cup apple cider vinegar
  • 2 tablespoons honey or agave
  • ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Optional: ¼ cup toasted sliced almonds for crunch

Step‑by‑Step Preparation

1. Shred the cabbage. Use a mandoline or a sharp knife to slice the green and red cabbage into match‑stick‑thin ribbons. Place the shredded cabbage in a large mixing bowl.

2. Prep the carrots. Julienne the carrots or grate them on the large side of a box grater. Add them to the bowl with the cabbage.

3. Mince the herbs with Herb Scissors. Gather the cilantro, chives, and basil in a small pile. Using the five‑blade Herb Scissors, snip through the herbs three to four times until they reach a fine, uniform texture. Sprinkle the minced herbs over the cabbage‑carrot mixture.

4. Make the dressing. In a separate jar, combine apple cider vinegar, honey, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Shake vigorously until emulsified.

5. Toss and rest. Drizzle the dressing over the slaw, then toss gently with tongs until everything is evenly coated. Let the slaw sit for 10–15 minutes; this allows the cabbage to soften slightly and the herbs to infuse the dressing.

6. Finish with toppings. If you like added texture, stir in toasted sliced almonds just before serving.

Tips for Maximum Flavor and Texture

• Dry herbs before snipping. Pat the cilantro, chives, and basil dry with a paper towel. Excess moisture can cause the herbs to clump.

• Don’t over‑mix. Once the dressing is added, toss just enough to coat. Over‑mixing can bruise the cabbage and turn the slaw soggy.

• Adjust acidity. If you prefer a brighter bite, add a splash more apple cider vinegar or a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

• Season gradually. Add salt in small increments, tasting as you go. The herbs already bring a natural saltiness.

Serving Ideas and Variations

This herb packed summer slaw works as a side for grilled chicken, fish tacos, or a backyard barbecue. For a heartier meal, fold in cooked quinoa or chickpeas. If you love a hint of heat, toss in a finely diced jalapeño or a pinch of red‑pepper flakes before the final toss.

FAQ

Can I use frozen herbs with the Herb Scissors?

Frozen herbs tend to clump and don’t mince well. Thaw them on a paper towel, pat dry, and then use the Herb Scissors for the best texture.

How long can the slaw sit before it loses its crunch?

For optimal crunch, serve within 2 hours of mixing. If you need to prep ahead, keep the dressing separate and combine just before serving.

Is the five‑blade design safe for home cooks?

Yes. The blades are stainless steel and positioned so that only the tips are exposed when you open the scissors. Always keep fingers away from the cutting edge and store the scissors in a safe drawer when not in use.
